title: Thursday, September 17, 2026

headline.title: “Price action is usually a lot better after FOMC.” That line was written on the prep sheet before the open yesterday, and this is what it looks like. Everything is green and the risk assets are leading: ARM +4.75%, AMD +3.20%, INTC +3.10%, MU +2.19%, NVDA +1.68%, with QQQ +1.41% and IWM +1.17%. The Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75–4.00%, the first increase since July 2023 — and the relief is not in the decision, it is in the dots.
headline.summary: The dot plot landed closer to one more hike than two, which is the half the market was not positioned for. Sixteen of eighteen participants expect another increase, but twelve of eighteen peg 2026 at an average of 4.125% — one more 25bp move — with only four seeing two. Futures had been leaning toward two by year-end. And the detail that says the most about this Fed: Warsh declined to submit a dot at all. A chair who will not place his own marker on the grid is telling you the committee's median is the signal and his guidance is not on offer. The tape read it as relief: gold +1.85%, bonds +0.76%, crude −2.25% — every part of that combination says less tightening ahead, not more.

overview:
Wednesday itself was not the relief; Wednesday was a grind. The S&P rose after the announcement but still closed −0.44% on the session, and the damage under it was concentrated in exactly the events this book had flagged. ON Semiconductor fell 9.02% on its own Analyst Day — the single worst outcome on the board and the clearest validation yet of the study's core finding that these events are volatility, not direction. INTU fell 6.20% the session before its own Investor Day, which is today. LEN closed −2.14% and then missed: EPS $1.19 against $1.28 expected and nearly half of what it earned this time last year, revenue $8.05B versus $8.23B consensus. The guidance is the worse half — deliveries fell 3% to 20,840 homes, Q4 is guided to 22,000–23,000, and full-year FY26 delivery guidance was LOWERED to 80,000–81,000 homes. The homebuilder read with mortgage rates north of 7% came in exactly as poorly as the setup implied.

Two enormous single-name moves this morning, in opposite directions, both on contracts rather than earnings. GNRC is +30.09% after securing a long-term Amazon supply deal tied to $8 billion in generator purchases, including $2.4 billion through 2028 — and Amazon took the right to buy up to $340 million of GNRC stock, which is the part that makes it a partnership rather than an order. Against it, FLNC is −22.21% after cutting full-year guidance to $2.4B from $2.9–3.1B and guiding to a $200M EBITDA loss against prior guidance of a $30M loss to $10M of EBITDA. Both are power-infrastructure names and they went opposite ways on the same morning — the data-center buildout is paying the generator maker and destroying the battery-storage one.

The crypto complex is repairing. COIN +2.85% and HOOD +2.78% after Wednesday's continued bleed (COIN −4.42%, HOOD −5.46%) in the wake of the failed CLARITY Act vote. NSC is +10.2% on filings showing more than 500 customers publicly supporting its proposed Union Pacific merger. And ARM +4.75% got a second CEO-on-television catalyst in a week: Rene Haas told CNBC he is increasingly confident the company can meet demand for its new data-center chip.

The central banks have already reported, and they did not move together. The Bank of England HELD at 3.75%, voting 6–3 — but Governor Bailey warned a hike is possible if the Iran conflict is prolonged, which puts a second central bank on the record saying the energy impulse is the binding constraint. Hong Kong followed the Fed with 25bp to 4.25%, and the Bank of Japan is expected to raise by 25bp tonight. Yields are confirming the relief: the 2-year is −5bp to 4.69% and the 10-year −5bp to 4.96% — back below 5% after Tuesday's 5.045% print. WTI is −1.7% to $100.66, and Trump is reportedly planning to meet Gulf Cooperation Council leaders next week, which is the first diplomatic date on the calendar since the Muscat talks were shelved.

Today: housing starts, building permits and the Philadelphia Fed at 7:30 CT, pending home sales at 9:00 CT and jobless claims at 9:30 CT — an unusual slot for claims. CCL reports before the open. The investor-day slate is the heaviest of the week — YETI, ASH, EAT, HUBS, ORLY and INTU all hold events, with INTU's the one carrying a real precedent. CRM trades ex-dividend today. And Friday is triple witching.

watchlist.em_label: MARKS VS WEDNESDAY 9/16 CLOSE — THE POST-FOMC RELIEF, AS THE SHEET PREDICTED

setups: Written down before the open yesterday

Yesterday's prep sheet carried one line in capitals: “PRICE ACTION USUALLY A LOT BETTER AFTER FOMC.” It also said the 1pm move is usually a fake out and to straddle the 1:30 presser rather than trade the decision. Both halves were right. Wednesday's session closed −0.44% — the decision itself produced nothing durable — and this morning the entire board is green with the highest-beta names leading. The mechanism was the dot plot: twelve of eighteen at 4.125% for 2026 means one more hike, not the two futures were leaning toward. The confirmation to watch is the combination: gold, bonds and equities all higher while crude falls is a coherent less-tightening trade, not a reflex bounce.

Every move in this argument for four sessions has come from someone talking — Amodei's essay, Huang's answer to Trump, Kurtz's post. This morning it finally has a price. CoreWeave says new compute capacity is being contracted at HIGHER prices, and Nebius is raising prices for its computing services — NBIS is +9.75% on it. Two AI-infrastructure names, same morning, both reporting pricing power. That is demand evidence, and it arrives nine trading days before MU's 9/30 print, which this book has been calling the first real number. The complication is inside CRWV itself: the same release sets up an at-the-market program to sell up to 35,000,000 Class A shares, and the stock is −1.52% on the combination. Higher prices for the product, more shares against it — NBIS got the pricing headline without the dilution, and the two tapes are pricing exactly that difference.

ON Semiconductor fell 9.02% on the day it held its Analyst Day. That is the cleanest evidence yet for the pattern this book has been tracking: sell-the-news ran four of five in our study, and three of five gapped up and closed below the open. The sheet had ON on watch with “entry straddle before market closes” — and a straddle is precisely the structure that does not care which way a 9% move goes. The directional version of this trade was a disaster and the volatility version was a winner, on the same name and the same day. It is +2.06% this morning, which changes nothing about the lesson.
The fade and the fundamentals disagree

This is the most interesting tension on the board. Salesforce's Investor & Analyst Session delivered: management said it is “confident” on a path to $63B in revenue in FY30, and the sell side responded overnight with a wall of raises — Stifel to $300, Canaccord to $300, Guggenheim to $300, BMO to $285, Mizuho to $280, Citi to $263, with JPMorgan calling the event positive for the “re-rating thesis.” And the stock closed −2.00% on the day of the event and is −1.71% this morning (it also trades ex-dividend today, which accounts for a small part). Our Dreamforce fade thesis is now right on price three times running and wrong about the substance. That is worth holding honestly: the pattern predicted the tape and said nothing true about the business.
The other side of the same trade

The cyber complex that was the green corner of Monday's board is being cut by the sell side this morning. PANW −2.17%, SentinelOne −3.45% and OKTA −2.16% all carry downgrades, and CRWD is −0.94%, its fourth straight session giving back the +13.85% Monday. Read the two halves together and the week has a clean shape: the AI-slowdown fear that created the safety bid is being unwound on actual pricing data, and the hedge against it is being marked down at the same time. The trade that worked on Monday is being dismantled from both ends. Note what is NOT in this: any company-specific bad news at any of the four.

prep.lead: ⚠ “I am a catalyst trader.” The sheet opens with the identity statement and the filter that follows from it: focus on targeted days, events, extreme volume and earnings — not on whatever the tape is doing. A second note at the top worth keeping: call flow in the money is buying shares, not a lottery ticket. FlowMS Zoom today. And the forward list is already written: next week's catalysts are PATH, ONON, MCD, QCOM, META and COST earnings — QCOM is +3.68% this morning into a Snapdragon Summit that runs 9/22–9/24.

darkpool.note: No fresh dark-pool tape in hand for this session yet. What stands from Tuesday night is the shape of the positioning into the decision: roughly $5B of S&P 500 tracker size, all bid-side — VOO $1.8B, IVV $1.7B, SPY $1.5B — and the mega-caps leaning the same way, with NVDA, AMD, MSFT, AVGO and AAPL all printing at the bid.
